question: An engineer adds a quiet synth layer under a chorus, and the chorus now sounds better. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the chorus simply got louder
How the layer sounds in mono
answer: Whether the chorus simply got louder. Side by side, the louder of two otherwise identical versions tends to sound fuller and clearer, even by a decibel, so any added layer starts with an unfair edge. Mastering engineers match levels before comparing. Turned down to the old level, many layers stop earning their place.
move: Before crediting a change, check whether it also changed the amount.
trap: Looking at what the layer plays, as if its content caused the lift.
reference: Katz, Mastering Audio: The Art and the Science, 2nd edn, Focal Press, 2007
